issues.description: The tensor-network zero-state function is named inconsistently across artifacts: the Problem Statement (and the Solution implementation) expect a function named create_zero_state(num_qubits) but the Template repository exposes a stub named init_zero_state(num_qubits). Specifically, problem_statement.md instructs students to implement `create_zero_state`, solution_repository/tensor_networks.py provides `create_zero_state(num_qubits)`, while template_repository/tensor_networks.py defines `init_zero_state(num_qubits)`. This mismatch will cause test harnesses or instructions that call or refer to create_zero_state to fail or confuse students because the template does not provide the expected entrypoint.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template and problem statement consistent. Rename the template function `init_zero_state` to `create_zero_state(num_qubits)` (preserving the same signature and behavior), or add a compatibility wrapper in the template: `def create_zero_state(num_qubits): return init_zero_state(num_qubits)`. Alternatively, update the problem statement and solution to refer to `init_zero_state`. Prefer renaming or adding the wrapper so tests and instructions that expect `create_zero_state` work without further changes.
